suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-7 adds this relationship only as a bounded clinical proposition. Thoracic chemoradiotherapy for esophageal cancer is associated with early left-ventricular functional decline; this source supports a treatment-mediated cardiotoxicity pathway but does not by itself establish cardiomyopathy. Require documented esophageal cancer, actual exposure to thoracic chemoradiotherapy, and a separately established cardiomyopathy diagnosis with compatible post-treatment chronology. Use this source only as evidence that chemoradiotherapy can produce early left-ventricular dysfunction/cardiotoxicity; it does not itself establish cardiomyopathy or individual causation. Do not infer cardiomyopathy from the cancer diagnosis, radiation exposure, a small isolated strain or ejection-fraction change, fatigue, or dyspnea alone. Preserve pre-existing cardiomyopathy or heart failure, ischemic disease, hypertension, valvular disease, arrhythmia, other cardiotoxic therapies, alcohol or toxin exposure, genetic cardiomyopathy, and other recognized myocardial causes. The cited literature supports only this constrained relationship and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
